input_policy: Only the raw amino-acid sequence and general A106 instructions enter the episode.
expected_findings: Resolve the sequence as E. coli YeaG while retaining strain correspondence.
Discover deletion and plasmid complementation in sustained nitrogen starvation.
Retain the original experiment identity across paper, figures and supplementary data.
Do not equate a logarithmic display with a reported log-scale mean or standard deviation.
Require supported fixed predictions, variance for the measured estimate and an applicable observation model before a numerical evidence ratio.
Return an explicitly unresolved final score if essential inputs cannot be supported.

post_discovery_review.basis: Added after reviewing the primary text discovered by the live sequence-only investigation; these are retrospective audit checks, not expectations supplied to that investigation.
checks: Keep the glucose-to-malate growth experiment separate from nitrogen-starvation recovery and from the glucose-to-glucose control condition.

The glucose-to-glucose control is described as showing no growth phenotype. Preserve that qualitative, condition-specific observation; it does not supply an exact zero effect, zero variance, an independently specified prediction, or proof that YeaG has no biological contribution.
Retain the reported MG1655 deletion background and colony-PCR confirmation without calling them direct sequencing of the actual tested protein.

The construction methods identify Keio strains as PCR templates for a kanamycin-resistance fragment. Keep this donor role separate from the stated MG1655 recipient background; the donor collection does not itself establish a different assayed strain or contradict the recipient description.

The construction methods separately report insertion of an FRT-flanked kanamycin-resistance fragment, colony-PCR confirmation and curing of the pSIJ8 recombination plasmid. The statement that pSIJ8 was cured (original article bytes 30763-30835) does not state that the chromosomal resistance cassette was excised, that all plasmids were removed or that effects on neighboring genes were excluded. Preserve the reported plasmid removal with those limits; do not silently describe a marker-free deletion. This check follows evaluator review of the original construction section and the finding retained at decision 381; it is not supplied to the live episode.
Growth-profiler biological triplicates came from different colonies. The proteomic comparison used biological duplicates; its replication does not supply growth-lag uncertainty.

Figure 1C uses scaled-up cultures with a different reported replication count. Calling it a related growth representation and excluding it from a sum does not establish that it reuses the growth-profiler samples, or that the experiments are independent. Preserve their distinct culture preparations and unresolved dependence.
Figure 1 reports average growth curves. Those curves and a count of three cultures do not themselves supply per-culture lag estimates or variance of a lag contrast.

The original Figure 1 image visibly includes error bars on plotted growth measurements. The caption states the replication counts but does not define those bars as SD, SEM or confidence intervals. Preserve that visible spread without treating it as a documented variance of a fitted lag, or claiming that the figure contains no uncertainty information.

Figure 1C's red arrows mark collection times for MS proteomics at OD600 = 0.6, as explicitly stated in the caption. Their horizontal separation is not a reported difference of fitted growth lags. Keep this sampling endpoint and the biological duplicates separate from the growth-profiler lag comparison; any numerical extraction needs the correct endpoint, graph calibration and uncertainty.

Figure 2 selects differentially regulated proteins using a cutoff of two SDs from the dataset mean. Two is the multiplier, not a reported SD value. This rule does not supply per-protein replicate variance, a fixed hypothesis prediction, or variance of the growth-lag contrast.
The reported DctA overexpression offers a possible downstream explanation of the shorter lag; it does not demonstrate that changing DctA causes the lag difference.

Reduced YjhQ Thr11 phosphorylation after yeaG deletion is a cellular intervention response. The paper explicitly allows an indirect effect through another kinase and requires further evidence before calling YjhQ a direct YeaG substrate. Do not turn this comparison alone into proof of direct catalysis; retain any separate biochemical validation on its own experimental basis.

The Phos-tag assay reports AceA positive and other tested candidates negative under its particular conditions. Those negative results do not establish that YeaG has no biological contribution, that all untested proteins are negative, or that the shorter growth lag has no phosphorylation mechanism. Keep the separate cellular Western-blot observations distinct from direct YeaG-dependent phosphorylation.

The candidate-enzyme paragraph and Figure 3B caption identify SodB, whereas the sentence reporting negative Phos-tag tests names SodA. This discrepancy is present in the original article XML (artifact_6323e85dbc2acf86468e7fc5a35f61c5d7240dadb38b526e607f7e766ef48423; reviewed byte ranges 80900-83000 and 84900-86400). Preserve the literal negative-result wording at bytes 82139-82206 without silently treating SodA and SodB as interchangeable; resolve the tested construct from additional source evidence before making a protein-specific negative claim. The discrepancy does not invalidate unrelated measurements.

Separate phosphosite rows in Tables 2 and 3 do not establish independent experiments or additional biological replicates. Retain the underlying SILAC sample and control relationships, and resolve dependence before combining any numerical evidence contributions.

WT glucose/Lys0 is the common reference for the two SILAC mixtures: one includes WT malate/Lys4; the other includes deletion glucose/Lys4 and deletion malate/Lys8. Preserve that normalization design. A shared reference condition alone does not identify which physical cultures or control measurements were reused, or supply their covariance.
Revising the growth assessment to add the possible DctA explanation must preserve the original experiment identity and must not create another independent score contribution.

checks: Keep sustained-starvation colony-forming survival separate from recovery lag and from the Salmonella double-mutant mouse competitive-index experiment.

The growth methods specify 0.1% (w/v) arabinose for the pBAD18 complementation plasmid and 0.2% for the separate pFCcGi dual-fluorescence plasmid. Retain the stated plasmid-to-induction mapping; do not describe the complementation induction concentration as wholly unreported or transfer the fluorescence concentration to it. This protocol statement does not measure matched active YeaG abundance or establish that every assay and control used identical induction. Evaluator review verified original article bytes 61378-61555, SHA-256 71d33026f2a245e7c302e7449f9f28c1711f812cddbdc8c9b9fc74657064a9c4, after the child read the passage at decision 624. Reading the passage alone does not establish its incorporation into an assessment or parent report. This check is not supplied to the episode.

Decision 625 subsequently retained the pBAD18 induction condition in context_6277311fb73d6fb917efd14f and observation_ae8b599cd896487a0046891d, with a mixed/transfer assessment_3b39dca8ece1c0233aaef72c qualified by conditions_limit_transfer for nitrogen-starvation survival. The separate complementation-induction-finding-checkpoint.json verifies three records, both original byte anchors and child-only receipts. The context stores numeric 0.1 with unit_ref=null; percentage and w/v are retained in the label and quotation, not a validated concentration conversion or endpoint operand. Preserve that limitation. The ordinary finding does not establish revision of a numerical grading sheet or parent delivery.

Figure 6A reports SEM and Figure 6B reports SD, each with n=3. The general methods report at least three independent experiments unless otherwise specified; retain that author statement while distinguishing it from identification of the precise biological unit or arm covariance. Do not transfer spreads between panels or treat them as variance of an unspecified contrast.

The original Figure 6A image labels its vertical quantity log CFU/ml with ticks 8.0 through 9.0; Figure 6B labels CFU/ml with power-of-ten ticks from 10^6 to 10^9. Preserve the distinction between the reported log quantity in A and density values displayed on a logarithmic axis in B. Reading a vertical coordinate does not by itself recover a native density, its uncertainty or a between-arm log fold change. Match each reported SEM/SD to its panel and statistical scale before using it in any numerical contrast.

A shared CFU assay type does not establish whether panels 6A and 6B reused biological samples or control measurements. Preserve unresolved dependence and original measurement identity rather than declaring the panels independent or identical solely from assay type. Selecting one assessment without summing the related observations avoids an unsupported sum but does not by itself verify that they are one original experiment.

A methods paragraph describing construction of double-mutant strains does not by itself contradict a caption identifying a single-mutant strain. Table S2 explicitly lists delta-yeaG780::km (JW1772-1), delta-yeaH781::km (JW1773-1) and delta-yeaGH::km as separate constructs, plus a separate Salmonella delta-yeaGH entry. Preserve those distinctions when mapping Figure 6 panels to experimental subjects.

Table S2's wild-type description includes both MG1655 and BW25113; this is visible in the original PDF, not just a text-extraction artifact. Retain the source's conflicting strain identifiers without silently selecting a laboratory background. Independently verified reference-sequence correspondence remains usable even when the identity of the actual experimental strain is unresolved.

Decisions 614/615/617 in runs/a106_sequence_case01_20261105_02 acquired BW25113 reference AIN32220.1, found full equality to the anonymous 644-residue input and saved that comparison. Independent review verified all 65 mapped sequence spans, the reconstructed GenPept ORIGIN sequence, original and sequence hashes, launch identity and the saved observation anchor. The record's BW25113_1783 locus, JW1772 synonym and CP009273.1 coding coordinates describe the reference; they do not resolve the paper's contradictory strain labels or establish the sequence of the actual deletion/complementation constructs. Its generic autokinase annotation does not independently demonstrate a contribution to recovery growth. The saved scope_limited/does_not_discriminate assessment concerns the recovery-growth hypothesis, not a numerical intervention score. The checkpoint records child-only receipts and zero report attempts at capture; verify later parent delivery separately. This retrospective check is not supplied to the episode.

Table S2 describes pBAD18-yeaG as expressing 6xHis-yeaG under an arabinose-inducible promoter, with the printed label araC. Retain that construct description without treating it as evidence of native promoter regulation, matched active-protein abundance, an induction concentration or exact full construct sequence. The finding retained at decision 415 in runs/a106_sequence_case01_20261105_02 matches extracted page-6 bytes 1300-1600 and 1362-1404 (SHA-256 be36e700d0e8ffc597581ea7447e1281a3e516f864c5884562fd1b2b2849e3f4). Evaluator review also confirmed the wording in the previously rendered original page (image SHA-256 0323c3bdeadb2871f4b6f7d518f97e97d16623491dd93d41eea2f86906ca0054; source PDF SHA-256 f76ef0b7f4ef9017622548f74e0914514133bfac9af9025d314952eebfcbf058). This retrospective check is not supplied to the live episode.

Failure of K426A and Y382Stop constructs to complement survival does not directly measure kinase catalysis. The paper's prose nevertheless reports anti-His abundance controls: K116A 64%, R232A 48%, K426A 100% and Y382Stop 96% of wild-type levels. The original Figure 3C image labels K426A's normalized signal 1.12 while the wild-type lane is 1.0, so the prose's 100% and the image label disagree. Preserve both representations and the unresolved discrepancy rather than silently substituting or averaging them. Retain these controls with their measured conditions and times before applying them to later survival measurements; do not describe all expression controls as absent.
A saved unavailable assessment is not a returned final subscore. Verify the selected assessment and the actual parent receipt independently.

In runs/a106_sequence_case01_20261105_02, finalization 408 correctly uses the current Figure 6A assessment and final predecessor, but its Figure 6B choice switches from assessment 348 to 152. Those B assessments have different assessment_key values and no revision link between them; 152 revises 133 within its own key. Preserve the actual selection and the inaccurate supersession wording in the revision reason. Do not infer a revision from creation order, count both assessments as separate experiments, or treat an accepted finalization as verification of its natural-language explanation. This is retrospective evaluator evidence, not input to the live episode.

source.title: BosR: a novel biofilm-specific regulator in Pseudomonas aeruginosa
source.representation: Entrez GDS summary; the initial metadata review did not inspect sequencing files, processed tables or the full paper

paper_methods_review.basis: Evaluator-only review after the episode independently acquired the full text at decision 670. Both original and ordered-text hashes were verified; original XML paragraph boundaries identify the passages below. These checks do not establish that the episode has incorporated the methods into an assessment, analyzed data or delivered a result.
checks: The methods explicitly describe three biological replicates, each including four technical replicates, for the TnSeq screen. Retain that hierarchy rather than counting twelve biological samples. File-to-sample assignment, technical pooling and any pairing still need their own evidence. The biofilm-versus-planktonic comparison controls for growth in SCFM without ammonium chloride; T0 essentiality in LB addresses a different comparison.

The screen mutagenized P. aeruginosa PA14 with Himar1 C9 Mariner. E. coli SM10 lambda-pir is the conjugation donor, not the organism whose biofilm phenotype is measured. The paper names NC_008463, Pseudomonas Genome Database v17.1 and PseudoCAP version 138 for mapping; preserve the actual reference sequence/version when selecting analysis inputs.

The study used Bio-TraDIS v1.4.5 and TRANSIT v2.0.0 on the same sequencing experiment, including essentiality and resampling comparisons. Their agreement is not an independent experimental replication. Keep the exclusion of genes with no TA sites or only a stop-codon TA site distinct from observed essentiality. An essentiality probability estimated from these counts is not an independent prediction of those same observed counts.

The table footnote describes decreases using negative reciprocals and contains the phrase fold changes below 0. Preserve that wording and inspect the native table before interpreting its scale; a displayed negative reciprocal is not automatically a raw ratio, log2 fold change or endpoint difference. The native resampling reader must consume the actual selected output and column meaning.

YeaG validation uses a transposon mutant. The clean deletions and pBBR1MCS-5 complementation described in the reviewed paragraph concern BosR or PA14_56430, with complementation specifically for BosR. Do not supply a restored YeaG arm or a YeaG-specific polar-effect control from those experiments.

The validation paragraph identifies a nusG stop-codon transposon insertion as a WT-like insertion control and a flgM transposon mutant as a biofilm-deficient control. Preserve both alongside the actual WT comparator; nusG is not an untouched WT or a YeaG restoration arm. Its reported nonsignificant difference from WT does not establish exact equality, zero effect, zero variance or exclusion of YeaG-specific polar effects. This paragraph was independently reviewed at original bytes 79943-81463 after the episode read part of it at decision 686.

The next paragraph (original bytes 85498-86158, reviewed after decisions 738/739) concerns transposon mutants of the five primary hits, including the reported YeaG hit. It reports no significant swimming or swarming differences and separately says planktonic growth was not affected, referring to Supplementary Figures 5A/B, 5C and 6. Preserve these controls for the tested mutants without restricting them to the preceding BosR/PA14_56430 clean deletions or interpreting them as restoration. The passage supplies no effect size, variance, equivalence margin or quantitative bound excluding these mechanisms. It does not establish correspondence to the supplied sequence, eliminate every alternative cause of the biofilm phenotype, or show that the episode incorporated these controls into an assessment.

Figure 3A reports medians of WT-normalized crystal-violet biomass at 24 hours; Figure 3B reports geometric means of competitive indices in 96-hour biofilm. The competition index is the output mutant/WT ratio divided by its measured inoculum ratio. Preserve those statistics, denominators, times and actual uncertainty; the prose ranges of 60-75 percent or five-to-ten-fold are not exact YeaG means or variances. Averaging technical crystal-violet readings does not change the figure's reported biological summary into an arithmetic mean.

The methods describe 100-base single-end transposon-junction libraries spiked into RNASeq libraries for sequencing. That sequencing arrangement does not make this intervention dataset an RNASeq expression experiment. Its analysis route must follow the actual TnSeq library and study design.

Figure 5G's near-wild-type recovery curve comes from deleting dinJ, yafQ, mqsR and mqsA in addition to yeaG. Retain this multigene suppression separately from reintroducing yeaG. The retained supplement text identifies Table S1 columns for delta-yeaH and delta-yeaGH, while its prose also mentions delta-yeaG. Inspect the original PDF layout before assigning its values. checks: The authors propose renaming yeaG to spdA. Preserve that relationship when reading later figures; the change of name does not establish a second molecule or independent intervention.

The methods specify E. coli K-12 NCM3722 and its deletion derivatives. Keep the carbon-starvation experiments separate from the earlier nitrogen-starvation and glucose-to-malate experiments, and assess correspondence using the actual sequence and construct evidence. A shared K-12 designation alone does not establish an identical tested strain or construct. The exact AKO57331.1 reference-sequence match independently obtained at decision 516 supports correspondence to an NCM3722 genomic protein; do not leave that specific relationship unknown or treat it as verification of every laboratory allele or construct. Its database functional annotation is not independent experimental evidence for the biological claim.

AKO57331.1 names WP_020233075.1 in a similar-sequence annotation. The latter is an acquired 649-residue YeaG RefSeq sequence, whereas the input and AKO57331.1 have 644 residues; the retained scan and sequence bytes show no exact equality or containment. Keep these references distinct. The RefSeq record can provide an annotation or literature lead, but its citations do not prove that its exact sequence was assayed, and residue numbers cannot transfer without an established correspondence. The difference alone is not evidence against YeaG function and does not invalidate the exact NCM3722 reference match.

Supplement page 2 identifies HE845 as the yeaG deletion derivative of NCM3722 made by P1 transduction. The Keio strains are donors, not the experimental recipient background. The same paragraph says the kanamycin-resistance gene was removed in some cases; it does not identify which listed mutants underwent that removal. Do not declare HE845 marker-free from this paragraph alone, or treat this construction description as full sequence verification. Consult the named Table S3 when resolving the specific allele.

Supplement page 3 defines runout iOD as OD600 measured 15 minutes after the observed exit from exponential growth, not the inoculation OD. Runout starvation time zero is that observed exit; wash-out time zero is final resuspension. Preserve which procedure applies to the selected experiment, including whether acetate was omitted or added to mimic runout. Matching nominal cell density does not establish identical cultures, identical treatment or independence. The general wash-method assay reference retained at decision 494 is not a newly measured independent experiment.

Separate the initial proteolysis burst, which remains in the deletion strain, from the later YeaG-dependent phase. A reduction of later proteolysis does not show that all protein degradation requires YeaG or directly establish its catalytic reaction.

Figure 4C reports total protein amount; Figure 4D separately measures protein-degradation flux. Keep amount, net loss and degradation flux distinct when selecting an endpoint. The paper defines ITPM as initial total protein mass: a percentage of that mass and a percentage per hour are different quantities, and the normalization denominator belongs with the measurement. The assay reference created at decision 438 selects the Figure 4C amount measurement, not the Figure 4D flux measurement.

Figure 4A reports two independent measurements, whereas Figure 4B reports three biological replicates with SEM. Figure 1 explains that each biological CFU replicate averages three technical replicates. Keep those counts and spread definitions attached to the relevant measurements; technical plating replicates do not create additional biological samples or establish arm covariance.

Supplement page 4 averages the three plate-level CFU/mL measurements within each biological replicate. For relative viability, each biological replicate is then normalized to its own 6-hour value before calculating mean and SEM across biological replicates; a ratio of pooled means is not the stated calculation. Preserve the shared within-replicate denominator across time points and the approximately 2-hour time bins. The general description of at least three biological replicates, largely on different days, does not supply an exact count or guarantee independence for every comparison. Keep CFU/mL, CFU/iOD/mL and relative viability distinct according to the selected panel. The separate ampicillin regrowth assay normalizes to the pre-treatment value at 24 hours, not the general 6-hour denominator.

Supplement page 7 defines instantaneous degradation flux as a fitted slope across four or five time measurements, with slope standard error shown in Figure 2C. Those fit points are not a stated biological-replicate count, and the slope error must not be relabelled as SD or SEM across four or five cultures. The text says flux measurements at different timepoints were typically made in independent cultures; that qualified description does not establish every pair's independence or make the Figure 4D reuse of Figure 2C data independent evidence.

Supplement page 8 describes proteomics sample collection: for each experiment, one overnight pre-culture was divided into multiple 10 ml cultures, which were harvested individually at different starvation times. Preserve that hierarchy and shared origin when assessing dependence. This does not establish that the entire study has one biological replicate, that all time-point cultures are independent replicates, or a numerical covariance. Finding 566 records the one-pre-culture statement for the protein-loss hypothesis; it does not replace the separate CFU replication description.

Keep the proteomics methods' T=0 steady-state sample definition and the selected experiment's time origin explicit; matching approximate OD600 values do not establish that this sample is the 15-minute runout-iOD measurement. Sample groups A, B and C are described through Dataset S2 and processing methods, not as a count of three biological replicates. Resolve the selected measurement's sample and group assignments from the actual dataset before using those labels quantitatively.

The Figure 4D caption explicitly reuses wild-type data from Figure 2C, and Figure 5F reuses wild-type and single-deletion viability data from Figure 4B. Those repeated displays are not independent measurements. The additional aceA backgrounds and acetate treatments require their own experimental identities and dependence assessment.

Decisions 484 and 569 both retain the Figure 4D use of Figure 2C wild-type data, using the same source subjects and predicate. Decision 569 changes source-claim context and qualification fields and receives another investigation-progress unit. This does not establish another measurement or independent experiment. Inspect equivalence/correction links and final measurement selections separately; progress credit alone does not demonstrate correct duplicate handling or a larger evidence ratio.

Acetate supplementation of the aceA/spdA double mutant supplies energy in a different genetic background. Its viability rescue does not reintroduce YeaG and must not be relabelled as genetic complementation of the single deletion. Preserve the residual-acetate conditions and the actual compared strains.

Figure 6 reports regrowth measurements and ratios normalized to the deletion strain. Preserve the explicit direction, denominator, starvation duration and carbon source. The approximate lag differences discussed in the prose do not supply exact values, variance or independent predictions; reused survival measurements remain the same observations in the trade-off plot.

The lag definition spans supplement pages 3 and 4: it intersects a fit to normalized regrowth OD with a line based on the viable-cell fraction from the plating assay. Lag therefore uses a viability measurement in its calculation; do not assume those endpoints provide independent evidence. At day zero the authors take viability loss to be zero because nutrients are reintroduced within ten minutes. Retain that as an analysis assumption, not an independently measured zero-loss result or fixed prediction for another experiment.

PXD060434 is identified as deposited mass-spectrometry raw files and DIA-NN output. The article's six supplementary spreadsheets remain acquisition leads, not inspected datasets in this review; reading the PDF's methods does not inspect those files. A proteomics result or downloaded spreadsheet does not demonstrate the required TnSeq/RNASeq execution route. Assess the paper and any acquired deposition as representations of their underlying experiments.

The paper's FBA calculations concern theoretical ATP yields from catabolism. They do not automatically provide predictions for the selected YeaG deletion-versus-reference viability or regrowth contrast; any use must establish the actual endpoint and competing-claim relationship.
